subject: zoology_2
question_text: What are the functions of liver?

verification.note: Sourced from 'My Baby Bullet-Q — Senior Inter Zoology' (Star-Q Pass Track Series, Sri Publishers, 2022), book p.29, SAQ 14. The printed exam years are the book's claim, reproduced here as appearances. Zoology-II holds only ONE source book in the corpus, so the two-book union check is structurally impossible for this card; 'not checked' does NOT mean 'checked and clean'. The mark split is our reading of the question and is a claim until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it.

insider_note: A list question. Number the functions — a paragraph hides the points and the examiner cannot tick them.

steps.label: Secretion of bile
steps.why: Bile is the liver's only digestive secretion, so it is the function an examiner expects first.
common_mistakes: Writing that bile contains digestive enzymes. It contains none.
Calling the liver an endocrine gland. Bile leaves through a duct.
steps.memory_tip: The liver is the biggest gland and bile is what it pours out.
steps.margin_note: Write this as a numbered list. The examiner ticks points.
lines: The liver is the largest gland in the body.
It carries out synthesis, storage and
secretion.
It secretes bile juice, which helps in the
emulsification and digestion of fats.

steps.label: Detoxification and heat
steps.why: Everything absorbed from the gut reaches the liver first, so it is the body's filter before the blood goes anywhere else.
common_mistakes: Naming the kidney as the chief organ of detoxification. It is the liver.
Leaving out the heat function. It is a marked point.
steps.memory_tip: Gut blood meets the liver first, so the liver is the filter.
steps.margin_note: Two short points, one line each.
lines: The liver is the chief organ of
detoxification. It removes toxic substances
that enter the gut with food.
It acts as a thermoregulatory organ and
gives out much of the body heat.

steps.label: Metabolism and urea
steps.why: The liver holds the enzymes of the ornithine cycle, so ammonia from deamination is turned into urea here and nowhere else.
common_mistakes: Saying urea is formed in the kidney. The kidney only excretes it.
Naming the wrong cycle. Urea is made in the ornithine cycle.
steps.memory_tip: Liver makes urea, kidney removes it.
steps.margin_note: Name the ornithine cycle. That word carries the mark.
lines: It plays the key role in carbohydrate
metabolism.
It takes part in lipid metabolism, making
cholesterol and triglycerides.
Deamination and the formation of urea by
the ornithine cycle occur in the liver.

steps.label: Blood functions
steps.why: The liver makes red cells before birth and destroys them after birth, so the same organ sits at both ends of a red cell's life.
common_mistakes: Writing that the adult liver makes red cells. In the adult it destroys them.
Leaving out the plasma proteins. Albumin and fibrinogen are marked names.
steps.memory_tip: Haemopoietic in the foetus, erythroclastic in the adult.
steps.margin_note: Close with Kupffer cells. It is an easy extra point.
lines: It is a haemopoietic organ in the foetus
and an erythroclastic organ in the adult,
destroying aged red blood cells.
It makes plasma proteins such as albumin,
clotting factors such as fibrinogen, and
the anticoagulant heparin.

lines.text: Kupffer cells remove microbes from the blood
